newsitem.title: USA: Sizzler emerges from bankruptcy protection.
newsitem.headline: Sizzler emerges from bankruptcy protection.

text.p: Sizzler International Inc on Monday said it emerged from Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection and expects to be profitable in fiscal 1998.

Sizzler said plans for reorganization of Sizzler International and its domestic subsidiary Sizzler Restaurants International Inc were approved on Monday by the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Central District of California.
"Our expectation is that fiscal 1998 will be a profitable year," Chris Thomas, president and chief executive of Sizzler's domestic operations, said in an interview.
The approved plan does not dilute shareholder equity or require the liquidation of any profitable operations.

Under the plan, Sizzler International will fully repay creditors claims of about $70 million, which will be secured by and paid from international operations. Sizzler Restaurants will repay in full creditors' claims of about $25 million which will be secured by and paid from domestic operations.
Sizzler filed for Chapter 11 protection last June, closing 130 unprofitable restaurants and taking a charge of $109 million. Since then it has terminated over 200 leases.

At the time Sizzler filed for protection, it was generating domestic losses of about $1 million a month. The bankruptcy was unusual because when Sizzler filed it had assets of $272 million and liabilities of just $98 million.
"Sizzler had become a dated concept with dated facilities and a dated menu and dated execution," Thomas said.

Over the past year Sizzler has introduced its American Grill concept menu which features healthier foods such as more grilled and smoked foods, including chicken and seafood, pasta as well as fresh fruit and salad. Such foods are viewed as more healthy than traditional steak house fare.
"We're going section by section in the menu and putting in new contemporary foods and flavors, higher quality ingredients as well as retraining the staff," Thomas said.
The company plans to renovate its restaurants to look more contemporary in the coming year.
"The niche that Sizzler resides in at the upper end of the mid-scale dining is wide open to us and we're going back out to capture those customers," he said.
On Monday the company began a new advertizing campaign in the Los Angeles and New York areas. About two thirds of the company's U.S. restaurants are in California.
In the coming year, Sizzler will focus domestically on growing same-store sales and plans to grow its international operations through franchising.

Sizzler has 69 company-owned restaurants in the U.S. and 199 franchised operations. Internationally, the company owns 39 restaurants and 97 franchises. It also operates 96 KFC restaurants in Queensland, Australia.
Sizzler competes with budget-priced chains such as Home-Town Buffet, Denny's and Coco's.
